answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake and require a small bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. When a counterparty proves fraud, the protocol slashes that bond and pays part to the reporter, so creating thousands of names multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. A raven can inspect a tundra route during a voyage, but each new agent still needs its own bond; the attacker pays upfront and loses it when caught.
